articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sheetal Devi, Swati Chaudhary storm into archery finals, eye gold medals for India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's para archers Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary stormed into the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026 on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's para archers Sheetal Devi and Swati Chaudhary stormed into the finals of their respective events at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, assuring the country of at least two medals and setting up opportunities to add to India's tally.Defending champion Sheetal continued her impressive run in the women's compound category, defeating Japan's Shinohara Aya 145-137 in the semifinal. The 19-year-old will face Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah in the gold-medal match on October 22.Swati, making her debut at the continental multi-sport event, also booked her place in the final after beating South Korea's Lee Eunhee 6-2 in the women's W1 semifinal. She will take on China's Mengkan in the gold-medal contest, with both Indian archers now assured of at least silver medals.Sheetal continues record-breaking runSheetal, who was born without arms and shoots using her feet and shoulder, has been one of India's standout performers in para archery. The Jammu and Kashmir archer equalled the world record and set a new Asian record during qualification, underlining her credentials as she seeks to defend her title.She continued her dominant campaign in the elimination rounds, defeating Hong Kong's Chan Yuen Wah 149-134 in the pre-quarterfinals and the Philippines' Agustina Bantiloc 147-135 in the quarterfinals before overcoming Shinohara in the last four.Sheetal had also produced a record-breaking 149 against Chan, surpassing the previous world record of 148 held by Britain's Jessica Stretton.The world No. 1 will now look to cap her campaign with another gold medal. She is also scheduled to compete in the compound women's doubles semifinals alongside Payal Nag.Mixed teams progress as India suffer individual setbacksIndia also advanced to the semifinals in both the recurve and compound mixed team events. Paralympic gold medallist Harvinder Singh and Bhawna defeated Thailand 6-0 in the recurve mixed team quarterfinals, while Sheetal and Toman Kumar beat Japan 154-147 in the compound mixed team competition.However, the day brought disappointment in several individual events. Harvinder lost 5-6 to China's Yun Duo in a shoot-off in the men's recurve quarterfinals, while Bhawna went down 2-6 to Mongolia's Selengee Demberel in the women's last eight.In the men's compound event, Toman suffered a 144-149 semifinal defeat to China's Ai Xinliang and will compete for bronze. Shyam Sundar Swami had earlier lost 146-147 to Ai in the quarterfinals.With Sheetal and Swati now one victory away from gold, India will look to convert their strong performances into top-podium finishes as the para archery competition progresses.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alemania, Francia e Italia se alían en contra de España para tratar de frenar la invasión de los coches chinos
articles.standfirst: Francia y Alemania, con el apoyo de Italia, se alían para frenar la ofensiva del coche eléctrico chino, pidiendo a Bruselas permitir los motores combustión más allá 2035 en contra de la opinión del Gobierno de España
articles.summary: Los tres grandes motores europeos se alían para frenar la ofensiva del coche eléctrico chino, pidiendo a Bruselas permitir los motores combustión más allá 2035 en contra de la opinión del Gobierno de España
articles.body: Alemania, Francia e Italia, las tres grandes potencias económicas de la Unión Europea, se han aliado para plantar cara a toda la oleada de coches eléctricos que viene de China y salvaguardar su propia industria del automóvil. En concreto, Alemania y Francia han ya alcanzado un acuerdo para exigir a Bruselas que revise el 'calendario de emisiones', de forma que se puedan seguir fabricando y vendiendo coches de combustión más allá de 2035. E Italia se ha mostrado favorable a buena parte de estas propuestas. En concreto, lo que quieren proponer es que en lugar de reducir las emisiones netas en un 100%, estas se reduzcan en un 90%, lo que daría margen a seguir vendiendo coches híbridos e incluso modelos sin ningún tipo de electrificación, aunque cuesta imaginar que para entonces se fabriquen coches que ni siquiera cuentan con una electrificación micro híbrida. No obstante, hay que tener en cuenta que la Comisión Europea ya había planteado reducir el objetivo al 90% en una propuesta presentada a finales de 2025, aunque con condiciones para compensar las emisiones restantes. Detras de este cambio de rumbo no se esconde una falta de conciencia medioambiental, sino una maniobra de supervivencia industrial. China domina todo el proceso de fabricación (lo que se conoce como la 'cadena de valor') de los coches eléctricos, desde el procesamiento de materias primas críticas (como el litio, el cobalto o el níquel) hasta la fabricación de materiales y baterías a un coste inferior al que tienen que pagarlas marcas de nuestro continente. Y eso puede poner en riesgo la supervivencia de la histórica industria del automóvil europeo. Pero también obedece a un interés por adecuarse a la realidad de nuestro mercado continental, en el que algunos países (España, por ejemplo) no terminan de aceptar del todo el coche eléctrico. En el caso de España, una de las razones que más pesa en su contra es el precio, fuera del alcance de muchísimos conductores. Pero también juegan en su contra una infraestructura de recarga que avanza muy despacio, además de otras razones como la necesidad de un garaje en el que tener un punto de recarga o la ansiedad que muchos sienten ante la autonomía. Ante este escenario, la disyuntiva abierta ahora mismo para la industria europea pasa por vender coches eléctricos con escaso margen de beneficio frente a rivales chinos o pagar multas millonarias por no cumplir los límites de emisiones. De estos tres países que promueven la revisión, Alemania y Francia lo hacen además con una intención estratégica de mutua conveniencia. Berlín consigue dar oxígeno a sus grandes fabricantes para que sigan rentabilizando la ingeniería de combustión, en la que han invertido muchísimo. Y a cambio París consigue el respaldo alemán para exigir que una parte mayoritaria de los coches sea de fabricación europea. Entre las propuestas se habla del 70% excluidas las baterías, lo que permitiría acceder a ayudas o incentivos. No obstante, la industria europea todavía no puede cantar victoria porque este pacto es de momento una intención, aunque muy firme. Para que las intenciones de este bloque se traduzcan en ley, la modificación que proponen debe ser debatida y aprobada en el Consejo Europeo y el Parlamento Europeo. Aun así, y dado el peso económico de Alemania, Francia e Italia en las instituciones, el acuerdo deja muy tocado el veto total al motor térmico y perfila un nuevo escenario en el que podamos seguir comprando coches con tubo de escape. Este acuerdo, por cierto, es contrario a la postura del Gobierno de España, que sigue apostando por mantenerse en el plan original dejando de producir y vender coches térmicos a partir de 2035.

articles.title: Who is Deepthi Jeevanji? Indian para-athlete wins 400m T20 gold with Games record
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Deepthi Jeevanji continued her impressive run in para athletics by winning gold in the women's 400m T20 event at the Asian Para Games on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Deepthi Jeevanji continued her impressive run in para athletics by winning gold in the women's 400m T20 event at the Asian Para Games on Tuesday. The Indian clocked a Games record time of 56.36 seconds to defend her title.The 23-year-old from Telangana finished ahead of Japan's Niina Kanno, who won silver in 58.92 seconds. Kanno's compatriot Akane Kato took bronze with a time of 1:00.26.Deepthi, who also holds the Asian record, has established herself as one of India's leading para-athletes with her performances at major international events.Who is Deepthi Jeevanji?Deepthi hails from a remote village in Warangal, Telangana. Her parents are small farmers who have also worked as labourers in their village. Her talent for running was spotted when she was young. According to her athlete profile, Sports Authority of India coach N Ramesh first noticed her during a state-level athletics meet when she was 15. He recognised her potential and began training her.Deepthi later received support from badminton great Pullela Gopichand. At his suggestion, she underwent testing for intellectual disability in Hyderabad.Her journey in para athletics began to gain attention after she competed at the Asian Youth Championships in Hong Kong in 2019, where she won bronze.From a village in Telangana to the international stageDeepthi continued to improve through competitions organised by the Athletics Federation of India between 2019 and 2022. She also won gold medals in the 100m and 200m events at the Khelo India Youth Games in Guwahati in 2020.Her breakthrough at the senior international level came at the Asian Para Games in 2023, where she won gold and set Games and Asian records in the women's 400m T20 event.She went on to win gold at the 2024 Para Athletics World Championships, setting a world record of 55.07 seconds. She also won a bronze medal in the same event at the Paris Paralympics in 2024.Deepthi added another achievement to her career by winning silver at the 2025 World Championships. She has also won gold at the Indian Open in 2025 and 2026.What is the T20 category?T20 is a classification for athletes with intellectual impairments. Athletes in this category may face challenges with processing information, concentration and following race plans or tactical strategies.The role of her parents in her journeyDeepthi's success has come with strong support from her parents. She has spoken about how they stood by her ambitions even when people in their village taunted them for supporting her sporting dreams.Their support, along with years of training and hard work, has helped Deepthi rise from a village in Telangana to the top level of international para athletics.Her latest gold at the Asian Para Games, achieved in a Games record time of 56.36 seconds, is another milestone in her remarkable journey.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cleveland Browns News and Rumors 10/20/26: Forget Them Picks
articles.summary: CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!THE DAILY BLOVIATIONI've rooted for many strange things in my years as a Browns fan. Karma...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

I've rooted for many strange things in my years as a Browns fan. Karma for Baltimore. TJ Watt going into pout mode. A swirling wind off the lake right as the other team's kicker lines up.

In 2026, I've added a new one. I root against the team Myles Garrett plays for. I don't root against Myles. I root against the Rams, which, given that Myles has been on IR since September, turns out to be a pretty fine distinction.

Back in June, the Browns sent Myles to Los Angeles for Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second and a 2029 third . The Rams did it for the reason the Rams always do it. Super Bowl LXI is at SoFi Stadium in February, and they live by a famous motto about draft picks that ESPN has to print as "F--- them picks." In September, The Athletic's Hope-O-Meter had Rams fans at 98.7 percent optimism. Browns fans checked in at 2.7.

I instantly figured the Browns first-round pick from LA was going to wind up being somewhere around the 31st or 32nd pick. With Aaron Donald coming out of retirement to play alongside Myles, the fate of the 2026 season seemed assured. The only hope, in my mind, that the pick would be higher relied on the dubious prospect of Rams QB Matthew Stafford starting to show his age.

Six weeks later, the Browns are 4-2 and tied for first in the AFC North. The Rams are 2-4 and dead last in the NFC West.

Bill Barnwell's autopsy at ESPN is worth your time if you enjoy reading about other people's problems, and I'm ashamed to say I do. The Rams lost the opener to the 49ers in Melbourne after they "tried to reimagine jet lag." They lost in Denver on a pick-six. They lost to Buffalo on Monday night when the special teams melted down. And on Sunday they lost 18-16 at home to a 1-4 Cardinals team, with Jacoby Brissett dropping back 35 times and never getting sacked.

The details are delicious, in a guilty sort of way. Matthew Stafford has gone from fourth in QBR last season to 14th. He has six interceptions in six games after throwing eight all of last year, and he ranks one spot below Deshaun Watson in passer rating, which nobody had on their bingo card in August. The defense built to terrorize quarterbacks has eight sacks. Total. Todd Monken was asked Monday why our defense is better without Myles. Smart man: " I'm not going to say that . You said that... I don't know that, because he's not here."

My favorite detail: the Rams' special teams ranked 32nd in DVOA through five weeks under coordinator Bubba Ventrone, who went to L.A. straight from Berea, where our special teams ranked 32nd last year. So we didn't just send them Myles. We threw in the kicking game at no additional charge.

Then came Monday, when Sean McVay read out an injury list that sounded like a casualty report. Davante Adams ruptured his hamstring and is out six to 10 weeks. Nose tackle Poona Ford is done for the year with a torn triceps. Kobie Turner is likely headed to IR with a groin injury. Blake Grupe, the kicker they signed after cutting the last one, tore his ACL in his debut, so they're working out Brandon McManus and Matt Prater today. And Myles, who had knee surgery in mid-September and has missed five games, won't practice this week.

Mary Kay Cabot summed it up: " First Myles Garrett, and now Davante Adams ." Zac Jackson was blunter: " The Rams are a mess and the Browns hold their first-round pick in 2027." And Jack Duffin has the math: the pick is currently No. 10 , and would be No. 5 if the Eagles hadn't, in Jack's word, "bottled" their Week 4 game against the Rams.

So the question I wanted to wrestle with this morning: does it continue?

My honest answer is probably not all the way, and I hate saying it. Barnwell makes a good case that a lot of this is bad luck. The Rams are sixth in the league in pressure rate but turn under 10 percent of those pressures into sacks, second-worst in football, and that won't hold with Aaron Donald in there and Myles eventually back. They've recovered four of 13 fumbles in their games. They're 1-3 in one-score games. And the schedule softens. CBS Sports has them at the Raiders, home against the Chargers, at Washington and at Arizona before their Week 11 bye, and favored in all four. Vegas has them as 5.5-point favorites in Las Vegas this week.

Then again, no team in the Super Bowl era has had a losing record after six weeks and won its conference. ESPN's FPI has dropped the Rams' playoff chances from 83.1 percent to 35.3, with less than a 1 percent chance of winning a division where San Francisco improved to 6-0 last night. After the bye, they get the Packers, Chiefs, at San Francisco, Cowboys, at Seattle, at Tampa and Seattle again. That's not a soft finish for a 38-year-old quarterback and a kicker to be named later.

Here's the part that matters to us. Non-playoff teams pick 1 through 18. If FPI is close, there's about a two-in-three chance the Rams miss the playoffs and that pick lands in the top 18. If they sneak in as a wild card, it slides into the 20s. If the wheels really come off, we're talking about a top-10 pick in a year the Browns are shopping for a quarterback, and Mel Kiper just told Arch Manning to " go back to college for another year ." If the shelf of available quarterbacks gets thinner, the extra first gets more valuable.

Which brings me to Marktroy's Watercooler thread: " The Rams will want Jeudy with Adams gone . Do you trade him?"

No. And not only because Monken said Monday, "We're better with Jerry than we are without Jerry," or because Daryl Ruiter notes Jeudy has helped win half the games that were on the line late. The last thing I want to do in October is sell the Rams a receiver. If Les Snead calls, Andrew Berry should let it go to voicemail.

So I'll be rooting for the Raiders on Sunday, which isn't something a Browns fan of my vintage says lightly after Red Right 88 was burned into my 17-year-old brain. I'm not rooting for anybody's hamstring. I'm rooting for Las Vegas. That's as low as I'll go.

44 YARDS, NOT 45: Monken on the first half against Baltimore: "I don't want 45 yards at halftime; maybe, I guess it's 44. I better not tack on a yard there." Scott Petrak has the numbers : Watson has been sacked a league-high 24 times and thrown only two interceptions, and his four fourth-quarter scoring drives tie Josh Allen and Bo Nix for the league lead. Watson: "One of these weeks it's going to click." I'd settle for the first quarter.

The Browns open as 1.5-point favorites at Tennessee with a total of 36.5. Vegas has watched our first halves. Monken says it's too early to tell on Mason Graham, Dylan Sampson, Quinshon Judkins, Mike Hall Jr. and Grant Delpit, per Fred Greetham .

QUICKLY: Fred has Monken on the "connected" defense , John Taylor has his Monday Morning Postmortem , and VIPs get Jack Duffin's Stock Up/Down and Sam Penix's Watson accuracy charting. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs, and our Crap Pile folder is already full of Shedeur-to-Philly speculation with nobody credentialed attached.

Have a good one! GO BROWNS! (And go Raiders. Just this once.)

Positive news from the world of sports and beyond...

Prime Video unveiled the new trailer at New York Comic-Con, and the eight-episode series lands Nov. 25. This time the replicants won the uprising and run the show, and they're the ones hunting humans. Michelle Yeoh plays Olwen, a fading replicant Blade Runner, who teams up with Hunter Schafer's Cora, a human on the run. Space.com is excited about the off-world planets and starships, and I'm excited about Michelle Yeoh in anything. It's set in a gloomy Los Angeles at the edge of the 22nd century where nothing goes right for the people in charge. Prime Video says it's fiction. I've been reading about the Rams all morning, so I have my doubts.

When not reading Bill Barnwell's Rams autopsy for the third time, Barry McBride is the Publisher and Founder of the OBR and bloviates this nonsense every morning. You can follow him on Twitter @barrymcbride or write him at barry@theobr.com if you are so compelled.

articles.title: Mathias Beck re-elected as president
articles.summary: Eintracht Frankfurt members have chosen Mathias Beck as club president again by an overwhelming result.In his election speech, Mathias Beck set out his visio...
articles.body:
Eintracht Frankfurt members have chosen Mathias Beck as club president again by an overwhelming result.

In his election speech, Mathias Beck set out his vision and aims for the next four years to the roughly 1,400 members in attendance. It will be Beck's first full term as president, having succeeded Peter Fischer two and a half years ago.

Beck painted a clear picture of how he imagines Eintracht in the coming years, the milestones he wants to hit and what is required to achieve them. With steady growth in the membership of the club's more than 50 sport sections and fan department, the 55-year-old is looking to reach the mark of 200,000 members. To support the growth in sport, particular attention will be paid to sports facilities infrastructure. He stressed that this will require cooperation with the State of Hesse and the City of Frankfurt.

Other key areas include the modernisation of the organisation, promotion of volunteering as well as social responsibility beyond the sport. With regards to professional football, Beck outlined the future path, emphasised the importance of collaboration between the e.V. (registered association) and AG (corporation), and spoke unequivocally in favour of the 50+1 rule.

"It's been a long and emotional evening," he said. "I thank the members for the confidence placed in me and the overwhelming vote. I perform this role and the duties involved with great enthusiasm. There is much to do in many areas of Eintracht. I have clear ideas about what I want to achieve with this club and with you in the coming years."

Treasurer hands over with record results

Vice-president and treasurer Dominik Berker provided the members with detailed insights into the 2025/26 financial year, which was hugely successful. The club achieved a net income of 2.7 million euros after tax – the highest ever. Crucial to that were increased income from the trade mark licence agreement, higher membership contributions and increased sponsorship income.

"Together, we have put the finances of our club on a stable footing in recent years and made important decisions for the future," summarised Berker in his final speech as treasurer. "I am stepping down from my post with the satisfaction that the club is in an excellent position, both financially and structurally; that the tax audits for previous years have been completed; and that the financial accounting system has been almost entirely digitised. Furthermore, we can report record turnover and a record annual profit." Berker had already decided before the general meeting that he would not stand for another term.

Executive committee set to remain in current form

Beck's executive committee should comprise current vice-presidents Moritz Theimann, Armin Kraaz, Stefan Minden and Benjamin von Loefen. In accordance with the articles of association, the vice-presidents are appointed by the election committee and the supervisory board, at the suggestion of the president and following the general meeting. A decision is expected by the end of October.

articles.title: ‘Nobody is…’ – Dave Portnoy points out ‘ridiculous’ decision by San Francisco 49ers
articles.summary: Dave Portnoy states his problem with one thing the San Francisco 49ers’ offensive unit does, which he finds to be quite meaningless. The San Francisco 49ers...
articles.body:
Dave Portnoy states his problem with one thing the San Francisco 49ers' offensive unit does, which he finds to be quite meaningless.

The San Francisco 49ers are the first team to win six straight games this season after they beat the Washington Commanders on Monday night. The team has looked quite unstoppable so far, with the defense locked in and the offence humming.

Kyle Shanahan is known to be someone who likes to build team culture around leadership and accountability. Many of the 49ers' stars have been with the team for many years now and take on important roles within the locker room. Dave Portnoy has a problem with one aspect of this.

Dave Portnoy calls out San Francisco 49ers for having five 'captains' on the offensive unit

The Niners have named five captains on offence this season. They are quarterback Brock Purdy, running back Christian McCaffrey, fullback Kyle Juszczyk, tight end George Kittle and left tackle Trent Williams. This includes the cornerstone pieces of the attacking unit, alongside their most senior members.

While the quarterback remains the leader, this group's overarching task is to ensure that everything about their offence functions smoothly. Considering that there are only 11 players on the field at one time for the O, though, Dave Portnoy thinks this is excessive.

"The 49ers have five captains on offence. Basically half their offence is captains. That's ridiculous. If everybody is a captain nobody is a captain," the Barstool Sports owner posted on X during Monday night's game.

While Portnoy has something of a point, making it about the 6-0 Niners is a bit absurd. They are one of the league's best teams, and their systems are clearly working. If he tempered his takes taking anything like that into account, though, he wouldn't really be the personality he is.

articles.title: New guide, new glory! Simran storms to Games-record gold as Tejalben adds bronze at Asian Para Games
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's Simran scripted a golden comeback at the Asian Para Games 2026, setting a new Games record to win the women's 200m T12 title with her
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Simran scripted a golden comeback at the Asian Para Games 2026, setting a new Games record to win the women's 200m T12 title with her new guide Shivam, while compatriot Tejalben Damor added a bronze to complete a memorable outing for the country on Tuesday.The 26-year-old Simran clocked 24.80 seconds to claim her maiden gold at the continental showpiece, finishing ahead of Iran's Hajar Safarzadeh, who took silver in 25.02 seconds. Tejalben, making her debut at the Asian Para Games, secured bronze with a time of 25.23 seconds.The T12 classification is for athletes with moderate visual impairment.Simran shines with new guide after difficult transitionA bronze medallist at the 2024 Paris Paralympics, Simran has been rebuilding her campaign with Shivam after her previous guide, Umar Saifi, was banned for a doping violation.She had won silver in the same event at the 2023 Hangzhou edition, making Tuesday's record-breaking performance a significant milestone in her comeback.Simran, however, admitted that fatigue and recovery issues had affected her preparations. Her personal Asian record of 24.46 seconds remained beyond reach, but she was delighted to secure the gold."My body was not feeling good, in fact, it felt tight because the recovery has not been great. I was very tired after my heat race," she said.The sprinter also spoke about the challenge of finding suitable vegetarian food at the Games, adding with characteristic humour: "Otherwise, we Indians can run on willpower too."Simran will next compete in the women's 100m, an event in which she won silver at the previous edition.Tejalben's bronze boosts confidence ahead of 400mTejalben's podium finish provided another boost to India's medal campaign. The 24-year-old said her journey had been shaped by financial hardships faced by her family and that she had arrived with considerable determination."My parents have struggled financially for most of their lives and I would even die to get a medal," she said.The bronze has strengthened her confidence ahead of the women's 400m, which she considers her strongest event."My next race is 400m and that is my best event and this medal has given me a lot of confidence for that event," Tejalben added.With Simran's gold and Tejalben's bronze, India enjoyed a double-podium finish in the women's 200m T12, highlighting the country's growing strength in para-athletics.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo blasted by former Manchester United boss : ‘He let the team down’
articles.summary: Former Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag has no love lost for Cristiano Ronaldo. A few years ago, before Ronaldo’s transfer to Saudi Arabia’s Al-Nassr,...
articles.body:
Former Manchester United manager Erik Ten Hag has no love lost for Cristiano Ronaldo . A few years ago, before Ronaldo's transfer to Saudi Arabia's Al-Nassr, he was with his former club, Manchester United. However, toward the end of his run with "The Red Devils," things started to get heated between him and Ten Hag.

However, their animosity ended with the departure of the duo. Now, years later, Ten Hag has reopened his feud with Ronaldo. The former Manchester United manager shared new details about the tension between the two and how Ronaldo let his team down.

Ten Hag assumed control at Old Trafford in the summer of 2022. In his debut season, he secured the English League Cup and later won the FA Cup in 2024, prior to being sacked in October of that year.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Speaking to The Athletic, Ten Hag opened up about his experience with Ronaldo and how the Portuguese player was behind the scenes. "He let the team down, and he let me down too, because we were planning for the season with him in it," Ten Hag said.

"I travelled to Portugal to speak with him about the objectives I was seeking to achieve before taking on the responsibility of managing Manchester United," he shared. "He is one of the best players in the history of football, and I respected him greatly, but as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and rely on the players I saw as the most suitable for the team," he explained.

In his interview with The Athletic, Ten Hag also discussed the shortcomings and Ronaldo's failure to reach his training levels. Currently, at 41 years old, Ronaldo is still going strong and has been representing both Al-Nassr and the Portuguese team.

articles.title: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reaches Edmond Open final, falls to Sloane Stephens
articles.summary: Redmond’s Kristina Liutova reached the Edmond Open W100 final in Edmond, Oklahoma on Sunday after returning to action last week for the first time since her...
articles.body:
Redmond's Kristina Liutova reached the Edmond Open W100 final in Edmond, Oklahoma on Sunday after returning to action last week for the first time since her first-round U.S. Open loss in September.

Liutova, 16, won her first four matches in straight sets before losing Sunday's final to 2017 U.S. Open champion Sloane Stephens, 3-6, 2-6.

Stephens, 33, had not won a title since April 2024. She reached a career-high ranking of No. 3 in 2018 and is now ranked No. 118 following Sunday's win.

Stephens has been working her way back up the tennis rankings after suffering a stress fracture in her right foot in 2025. Earlier in her career, she suffered a similar injury in her left foot.

By reaching the Edmond Open final, Liutova climbed six spots in the rankings to No. 110.

Kristina Liutova's Memphis Classic breakthrough

Liutova entered the Memphis Classic over the summer ranked No. 229 in the world. She fought through qualifying and won the tournament, becoming the youngest active WTA champion and the first person born in the 2010s to win a tour-level event. It was the first tour-level event she had ever played.

Liutova's mother, Elena Morozova, said her daughter has been competitive since birth.

"Even when she played hide-and-seek, she wanted to win every time. Even when she played chess with her dad, she wanted to win every time," Morozova said. "In everything she was doing, she was trying to win."

On the court, Liutova doesn't focus on results. Her mentality is to put in the work and let the scoreboard take care of itself — the same mentality as her tennis hero.

"My favorite tennis player has always been Rafael Nadal, for his composure, for his hardworking character," Liutova said. "He's been through a lot of injuries, and the character is just shown in everything. He is just a great human as well, off the court. Always humble. Just an incredibly inspiring person and player."

Liutova is keeping her overall tennis goals and dreams private for now. But she wants to inspire others and take care of her mom, who has sacrificed so much to get her where she is today.

"I want to make sure that she's happy, and in the future, she has an easy life — a house, a cat — and just watch my matches with no worries and no pressure," Liutova said.

Liutova's U.S. Open run ends against Zheng Qinwen

After Memphis, Liutova won three U.S. Open qualifying matches in New York to reach the main draw . There, she faced 2024 Olympic gold medalist Zheng Qinwen. Liutova couldn't hold off the veteran, falling 4-6, 6-3, 6-1.

Liutova left the court in tears after her nine-match winning streak ended.

ESPN match commentator Robbie Koenig offered Liutova words of encouragement.

"I'll tell you what, there will be a lot more tears of joy in the years to come," Koenig said after her U.S. Open loss. "That's for sure, given the game that she possesses. Don't worry about that, Kristina."

Kristina Liutova makes Grand Slam main-draw history

Liutova fought through three qualifying matches to earn a place in the U.S. Open main draw.

"[She's] just so accurate with her ball striking," Koenig said of Liutova early in the match. "I'm gobsmacked that she's just 16 years of age."

Liutova is the first player born in the 2010s to qualify for a Grand Slam tournament's main draw. She was also the youngest person in the draw.

"Honestly, I never look at the stats," Liutova told KIRO Newsradio before the U.S. Open. "When I get told, I forget immediately."

Zheng acknowledged the teenager during her post-match ESPN interview.

"I want to say congratulations first to the opponent because she's only 16 years old," Zheng said. "Very young junior, and she played incredible tennis. Fights a lot. It was not easy for me."

Frank Lenzi is the News Director for KIRO Newsradio. Read more of his stories here .

This story was originally published on MyNorthwest.com.

articles.title: Crimson Crank: Nitpicking Indiana’s 19-15 loss to Ohio State
articles.summary: The problems that led to Indiana’s loss to Ohio State, largely on offense, had been brewing for weeks before the game.
articles.body:
Indiana suffered its first loss since 2024 on Saturday afternoon, falling to Ohio State 19-15. It was a hard-fought game between two evenly-matched teams, as reflected by the the fact that the Hoosiers fell just one spot in the latest AP Poll.

Because of how winnable the game was, fans and media alike have spent much of the last two days trying to figure out who to blame, particularly for Indiana's final offensive play. After struggling for most of the day, Josh Hoover threw a ball that was good, but not great, to Nick Marsh, who caught it with his feet out of bounds to effectively end the game.

It's a painful play to revisit, even as I sit here thinking about it Monday evening. But was that really what cost Indiana the game? Not really.

I was critical of the passing game on Saturday because the accuracy issues predated the Ohio State game. Indiana punted four times, in addition to the two field goal tries, because drives kept stalling out when Hoover missed passes. Any one of these could have ended in the touchdown that would have won the game for the Hoosiers.

Then there are the missed field goals. Radicic missing an easy one had an immeasurable impact on the game. Had he converted from 32 yards out, Indiana's final drive wouldn't have had to end with a shot at the end zone. The drive could have been planned around just getting into Radicic's normally consistent range.

It's not fair to blame Radicic for the miss from 55-yards, but it's another play – more so than the Hoover's last pass – worthy of a closer look.

After the Nebraska game, I questioned whether Cignetti had lost some of the aggression that made last year so special. The decision to kick down six from well beyond Radicic's career-long only makes me worry more.

Because Radicic had never really given us reason to think this was in his range, I struggle with calling this the "safe" call from Cignetti. It's kind of just a head-scratcher.

I watched Indiana's offense on Saturday, like everyone else, so I do understand lacking confidence in execution on a crucial fourth down play. That said, there are going to be other high-leverage plays this season that the offense will need to execute on, so they may as well practice now.

With how much Indiana has struggled to run the ball the last few weeks, the staff may have felt somewhat handcuffed in play-calling, which could have impacted the decision. The defense was also playing well, making a turnover feel less threatening in that scenario.

Saturday's result, though, demonstrates that offenses have to make plays to win games. Whether it's Hoover settling down and making passes that he's capable of making, or Mike Shanahan retooling the run game to get Lee Beebe Jr. and Turbo Richard some better looks, it's not a problem Indiana can shy away from.

I don't pretend to have an answer, but taking a step back from Saturday makes it clear that the loss has more to do with issues that have been plaguing Indiana's offense well before the Buckeyes got to town. If Indiana can clean these things up and string together more scoring drives, there will be no reason to litigate single incompletions.

articles.title: Indiana’s Malia Samuels lands NIL deal with World’s Finest Chocolate
articles.summary: Indiana Hooiser Malia Samuels explains why her new NIL partnership is so important to her.
articles.body:
Many college athletes view NIL deals as opportunities to support good causes.

Indiana women's basketball player Malia Samuels' new NIL deal with World's Finest Chocolate is one of those feel-good stories of giving back.

World's Finest Chocolate is a fundraising company that helps schools, sports teams, clubs, and community organizations raise money by giving youth the opportunity to sell chocolate. From third to fifth grade, Samuels sold WFC's chocolate to fund travel basketball opportunities and follow her dream.

Now she is a "Reign Maker" for the company's "Let Them Reign" campaign.

She is the first female college athlete to partner with the brand.

As explained by the CEO of World's Finest Chocolate , Eddie Opler, in a press release:

"Let Them Reign" was created to celebrate the ambition behind fundraising and the experiences it can help make possible. Having Malia join us as our first female NIL partner marks an important chapter for the campaign. We're proud to have her represent what can happen when determination, opportunity, and support come together.

The campaign focuses on encouraging youth to develop confidence, communication skills, resilience and entrepreneurial thinking while selling the chocolate.

Samuels herself used her childhood experience with World's Finest Chocolates to break out of her shell and improve her communication skills.

The basketball it allowed her to play led to her becoming the No. 1 recruit from her home state of Washington in 2023. In high school in Seattle, she won two state championships and received the 3A Washington State Player of the Year award as a junior in 2022. After three years at USC, she is excited to suit up for the Hoosiers in 2026-27.

Samuels took the time to speak with Swish Appeal about the deal.

Yeah for sure, it was definitely gratifying, kind of to help my parents out. And I think it was more so fun for me to do than thinking about, "Oh I have to do this to play travel basketball." It was just something that me and my teammates would kind of try to compete and see who could sell the most chocolate and stuff like that. But looking back, it was definitely gratifying.

Yeah for sure. I think basketball has always been such a big part of my life. And without the travel basketball piece from when I was really young, I wouldn't be where I'm at now. So I do have a lot of gratitude toward World's Finest Chocolate for making that happen for me.

I think I've always tried to use my NIL for a good cause, whether that be my camps that I did last year or finding a good cause to give back to my community. Just because the high school that I went to was in a kind of rough area of the city. I want kids to kind of like see themselves in me and want to do this when they get to my age and give back to kids. I want the generations to just keep building on each other and giving back to each other.

I think for me, it taught me skills that I didn't realize were so valuable. Like communication, confidence and resilience. Being ok with some nos because ultimately some nos will lead to some yeses. I think it's very important to teach kids those skills at such a young age. I think COVID kind of messed that up for some kids and their development. So I think it's important to really hone in and focus on the fundamental skills that kids need now.

I think it's super significant, and I think for me it has even more significance because I was on a boys' basketball team when I did sell chocolate. There weren't like a ton of girls around playing sports. There weren't a lot of girls that took basketball seriously at that age. So I had to play with the boys.

So it's super significant for girls to get more opportunities, for women's basketball to get more popular. Having the opportunity to travel and do all these things with basketball, it kind of shows girls all around the world that, "Oh this is really something." And that's kind of my basketball story. Like, "Oh I can go to college and play basketball?" Like, I never knew that. So I think that's kind of what I want to be for the next generation of girls by doing this.
